label: GO after unrewarded a2, growing with episode time and belief S2 is good
terms: (phase == GO) * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(-belief_lo, -5, 5) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.clip(-belief_lo, -5, 5) * ep_trial ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0)
explanation: Active only at GO, and essentially only when the previous trial was a2 unrewarded (residual +0.59 after a2 S1 u (rare), +0.26 after a2 S2 u (common); about -0.10 after every other pattern, i.e. near zero). Magnitude grows with episode trial (near 0 early, up to ~1.5-2 late in the episode), more steeply after the rare a2 S1 u loss. Within a2-unrewarded trials it is larger when the ideal-observer belief favours S2 being good (graded -belief_lo, interacting with episode time), i.e. a loss on a2 that does not overturn the belief S2 is good (a stay-on-a2 signal). A second consecutive unrewarded a2 trial reduces it substantially (weight -0.24), consistent with the belief weakening. Observed-only terms; no future or model-output variables. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.63 (dev 0.63), above the profile all ceiling 0.44 because of the episode-time and belief interactions; last-trial table alone gives 0.35. Not checked against the earlier model-value explanation score directly; the policy-decile table alone gives only 0.11, so observed quantities appear to lose little.

issues: The original terms all require prev_action == 2, so they never fire on the first trial of a window, where prev_action is -1 even though prev_reward is known. Misses shows 'GO after ?' as the most under-predicted class (+0.073); one worst window has actual 1.96 against predicted 0.098 at t83. Letting those steps in with isin(prev_action, [2, -1]), or with separate prev_action == -1 terms, raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.63 to 0.67-0.69. Part of this comes from how the windows are cut, but it is a systematic error class.

The magnitude falls more steeply over a run of consecutive a2 losses than the single 'second loss in a row' term (-0.24) captures. Late in the episode, after a second or third loss in a row, actual values are often 0 where about 1.2-1.6 is predicted (e.g. t96-t99 and t75-t77). The agent still chose a2 on these trials, so 'stay on a2 despite this loss' overstates things: the feature goes quiet on later losses in a run while the agent keeps staying.

'Grows faster after the rare a2 S1 u loss' holds only marginally. With rare and common alone, the slopes on ep_trial are +0.016 vs +0.006. With belief in the model, the original fit gives rare 0.0049 vs common 0.0106 per trial, and my fit gives a negative rare*ep_trial weight (-0.004). The rare advantage is carried by the belief shift, not by a separate effect of the transition.

The belief claim checks out: belief-binned terms among unrewarded a2 trials have monotone slopes on ep_trial (belief < 0.1: 0.020; belief > 0.75: about 0). The signed -belief_lo main effect is negative and only the interaction with ep_trial is positive, so 'larger when the observer believes S2 is good' is true mainly late in the episode.
The loss from going observed-only was not measured. 'The policy-decile reference alone gives only 0.11' is weak evidence that the loss is small.
Test 0.629 vs dev 0.63 reproduced. The feature is zero at D1 and D2. Other previous-trial patterns sit at about -0.10 (the intercept offset). These claims check out.
